name: SPIRITS 16ln
galaxy: M33 (giant HII region NGC 604), d=0.84 Mpc
pos_source: Gaia DR3 303386770278587776 via SIMBAD (coo_qual A). HST/ACS position (Garofali+2019 Table) 01:34:32.615 +30:47:04.178 and Spitzer position (Lau+2021 Table 1) 01:34:32.61 +30:47:04.3 agree to <0.15"; Lau+2021 Spitzer-HST 1-sigma error circle 0.165". SIMBAD: 'SPIRITS 16ln' and 'SPIRITS16ln' resolve to the same object as '[GLM2019] N604-WRXc' (the bare string 'N604-WRXc' is not a SIMBAD identifier).
amp_notes: Spitzer/IRAC (Lau+2021): quiescent 2003.99-2006.10 F3.6=632+/-30 uJy, F4.5=597+/-26 uJy; brightest observed 2015.24 (MJD 57111.7, first SPIRITS epoch, already fading) F3.6=973 uJy, F4.5=979 uJy => excess ~+340 / +380 uJy; 711/682 uJy by 2016.28. Quiescence-subtracted peak M[3.6]=-9.8, [3.6]-[4.5]~0.6. True IR peak lies somewhere in the 2006.10-2015.24 Spitzer gap; X-ray (0.5-2 keV) peak 2006.44 (2006 Jun 9, Garofali+2019), Lx~3e35 erg/s.
classification: WC4 + O colliding-wind binary candidate (X-ray bright); episodic dust maker

refs.note: Lau et al. 2021, Revealing Efficient Dust Formation at Low Metallicity in Extragalactic WC Binaries (Table 1 positions, Table 3 classes/periods, Table 6 IRAC light curves); period constraint 8.8 > P > 2.2 yr
Garofali et al. 2019, First candidate colliding-wind binary in M33 (HST position, WC4+O spectrum, X-ray light curve)

confidence_notes: Identification secure (Lau+2021 claim SPIRITS 16ln = N604-WRXc). Period only bounded; the single recorded IR peak epoch is a lower bound on the true peak date. WISE caveat: inside NGC 604, a very bright extended HII region; HST neighbours N604-WRXa (0.45") and WRXb (0.6", brighter in optical) are unresolved. Note: Oddsky H-0012 already flagged an 'obscured-transient' 0.2" from this object (triage CSVs).

name: SPIRITS 19q
pos_source: Lau+2021 Table 1 Spitzer position 07:37:18.21 +65:33:49.0 (repeated in Lau/2026 JWST paper); SIMBAD same (coo_qual D, from Lau+2021). Quoted to 0.01 s / 0.1"; true accuracy ~0.3" (Spitzer).
amp_notes: Spitzer (Lau+2021): quiescent 2004.77-2017.03 F3.6=345+/-9 uJy, F4.5=326+/-8 uJy (cluster/HII blend, M[3.6]=-12.73). Rise first seen 2017.48; peak 2018.47 (MJD 58288.9) F3.6=1738 uJy, F4.5=1980 uJy => excess +1393 / +1655 uJy (M[3.6]=-14.49, M[4.5]=-15.12); fading ~0.4 mag/yr (3.6) and ~0.3 mag/yr (4.5) to 2019.58. unWISE forced photometry (2026 JWST paper, Table 1): baseline W1~3.05 mJy, W2~4.95 mJy (larger blend); peak 2018.20 (MJD 58189.9) W1=4.62, W2=8.35 mJy => excess ~+1.6 / +3.4 mJy; still above baseline in 2024.2 (W1 3.36, W2 5.37 mJy). Dust mass 6.6e-6 Msun.
classification: WC4 (early-type WC) binary candidate in luminous cluster (M_V~-9.5); WC association with the outburst confirmed by JWST/NIRSpec IFU (2024 Apr)

refs.note: Lau et al. 2021, Revealing Efficient Dust Formation at Low Metallicity in Extragalactic WC Binaries (Table 1 positions, Table 3 classes/periods, Table 6 IRAC light curves); P >~ 12 yr (quiescent 2004-2017)
SPIRITS 19q: JWST/NIRSpec confirmation; includes unWISE W1/W2 light curve 2010-2024; assumes min. period 12 yr
JWST GO 1863 proposal (Lau), context only

confidence_notes: Best-characterised single outburst in the sample and the one with a published unWISE light curve: an ideal positive for a WISE detector (only one cycle, so it tests detection, not recurrence). Caveat: Oddsky H-0012 matched a Gaia source (DR3 1089774769415015552, plx/err 4.7) at this position and labelled it 'foreground star'; 19q sits in a luminous compact cluster, so that parallax is probably spurious. A foreground-star veto would wrongly reject this known object.

galaxy: NGC 6946 (3.9" from HII complex NGC 6946-26), d=7.72 Mpc
classification: Early-type WC (WCE: C IV 5801-12 and C III/He II blend, no C III 5696); episodic? dust maker

refs.note: Lau et al. 2021, Revealing Efficient Dust Formation at Low Metallicity in Extragalactic WC Binaries (Table 1 positions, Table 3 classes/periods, Table 6 IRAC light curves); variability 'Episodic?', period '?'

name: SPIRITS 14bqe
pos_source: Lau+2021 Table 1: 01:05:01.95 +02:08:51.3; SIMBAD same (coo_qual D). Spitzer 2-sigma positional uncertainty 0.6"; point-like WIRC Ks counterpart; a second NIR source sits 1.8" SE (no mid-IR emission).
amp_notes: Lau+2021: two outbursts with equal peaks: 2010.12 (MJD 55241) F3.6=107, F4.5=189 uJy and 2018.89 (MJD 58443.65) F3.6=104, F4.5=188 uJy; quiescence F3.6=63, F4.5=82 uJy => excess ~+44 / +107 uJy (+0.6 / +0.9 mag at 3.6/4.5). Fades back over ~2 yr. Colour 0.77 (quiescent, persistent dust) to 1.10 (peak). M[4.5]=-9.35 at peak. The peaks in Table 6 are 8.77 yr apart, the paper quotes ~8.5 yr, and the 2018 peak is poorly sampled (2018.34 to 2019.27). The single 4.5 um point at 2003.97 (115 uJy) sits above quiescence, perhaps the tail of an earlier ~2001-02 outburst (my inference). Extrapolated next peak ~2027.4-2027.7 (my extrapolation).
classification: Unclassified dusty IR source (no optical spectrum); candidate persistent + episodic dust-forming WC binary; Z~0.16 Zsun. NIR M_Ks=-6.4 matches dusty WC9 stars

refs.note: Lau et al. 2021, Revealing Efficient Dust Formation at Low Metallicity in Extragalactic WC Binaries (Table 1 positions, Table 3 classes/periods, Table 6 IRAC light curves); 'Episodic', P~8.5 yr (two peaks)
Massey et al. 2021: IC 1613 has only one known WR star (a WO); footnote cites 14bqe as a possible dust-forming WC binary

confidence_notes: The only extragalactic candidate within 10 Mpc with two observed recurrences. It is also nearby (0.72 Mpc), isolated and point-like, so it is the best periodic positive for a WISE recurrence test. Its WR nature is unconfirmed (no spectrum, and Massey+2021 counts no WC star in IC 1613). The period rests on two peaks.

name: HD 36402
amp_notes: WISE/NEOWISE (Williams 2019 Table): W1 9.25 (2010.91, near max) / 9.29 (2016.41, max) to 10.18 (2018.88), so dW1~0.93 mag; W2 8.38/8.43 to 9.33, so dW2~0.95 mag. W1-W2 stays ~0.85-0.87: dust is always present (variable, not purely episodic). Rise and fade ~1.5 yr each. Williams+2013: IRAC/WISE rises in 2004-05 and 2009-10, interval 4.7+/-0.2 yr; old near-IR ephemeris T=1996.9+4.7N (superseded). Projected maxima with P=5.11 yr: ~2021.5, ~2026.6 (my projection).
classification: WC4(+O?) + O8I: probable triple; inner WC4+O 3.03-d binary, dust period presumably the outer O8I orbit; dust maximum near X-ray minimum (colliding winds)

refs.note: Williams et al. 2013: variable dust formation, P~4.7+/-0.2 yr
Williams 2019: NEOWISE-R; period revised to 5.11 yr (WISE alone 5.2 yr); max early 2016
Williams et al. 2011: heated dust, ~800 K; two luminous YSOs nearby

confidence_notes: Secure periodic dust maker. Not within the 'nearby galaxy' WISE regime (LMC, bright W1~9-10, well detected). Caveat: two luminous YSOs nearby (Williams+2011) can blend at WISE resolution. No error is published for the 5.11 yr period; the earlier 4.7 yr value had +/-0.2 yr.

name: HD 38030
galaxy: LMC (~23' from R136/30 Dor), d=0.05 Mpc
amp_notes: WISE (Williams+2021 Table): flat 2010.31-2017.77 at W1~12.70, W2~12.53; rising 2018.31 (12.00/11.26); max 2018.76 W1=11.52, W2=10.62 (dW1=1.18, dW2=1.91 mag); fading 2019.31-2020.76 to 12.60/12.08. Dust colour temperature ~830 K. Ks quiescent 2000-2010. Interval >20 yr; a possible 1996-97 DENIS brightening would imply ~22 yr (doubtful).
classification: WC4 + O9.7III-IV companion (absorption lines, RV shift of C IV); episodic colliding-wind dust maker like WR 140/WR 19

refs.note: Williams 2019: discovery of the 2018 NEOWISE-R dust episode
Williams et al. 2019 RNAAS: preliminary report with light curves
Williams et al. 2021: O9.7 companion, full WISE history 2010-2020, interval >20 yr

confidence_notes: Secure single episode (one cycle), so it tests detection rather than recurrence. No X-ray detection (Chandra).
